global_influences.artist_or_genre: Pearl Jam / Alice in Chains / Soundgarden / Stone Temple Pilots
global_influences.evidence: All band members are explicitly documented as greatly influenced by 1990s American grunge/alternative rock, specifically citing Pearl Jam, Alice in Chains, Soundgarden and Stone Temple Pilots as core inspirations.

local_adaptation_notes: Indalo is a direct 'supergroup' formation drawing members from three previously-catalogued bands — Jon Kabir from Black, Zubair Hasan and Ahsan Titu from Aashor (Titu also of Black), and Dio Haque from Nemesis — making it a clear case of cross-band genealogical convergence within the Bangladeshi alternative rock scene; the 2021 EP 'Notun Khaame Purono Chithi' is explicitly framed as a tribute to legendary local artists, directly acknowledging the scene's own history within new material.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (2012): formed by Jon Kabir (Black), Zubair Hasan (Aashor), Ahsan Titu (Aashor/Black) and Dio Haque (Nemesis); first public performance 10 November 2012. Early lineup churn: Titu departed after recording debut single 'ISD,' replaced by Bart Nandit Areng; Dio Haque took a break after a heart attack and stroke, with Mubarak Milon and later Quazi Farhan filling in on drums before Milon's return. Debut album period (2015): Kokhon Kibhabe Ekhane Ke Jane established the band's grunge-influenced alternative rock sound. Later period (2021): EP Notun Khaame Purono Chithi paid tribute to legendary local artists; a second album (Uttor Khujchi Dokkhine) was recorded but remains unreleased.

listener_community_notes: As a cross-pollinated 'supergroup' drawing from Black, Aashor and Nemesis, Indalo functions as a direct node connecting multiple alternative-rock fan communities within the BMPN preference network; its members' documented health-related lineup disruptions (Dio Haque) also illustrate the human/biographical continuity challenges facing long-running Bangladeshi bands.
